title: Sellier SA – investment in Tannerie Morel (N and N+1)
text: On 1 January N, Sellier SA, which prepares IFRS consolidated financial statements, acquires 35% of the shares of Tannerie Morel for €42 million in cash. The investment gives Sellier two seats out of seven on the board; Sellier does not control Tannerie Morel. On that date the fair value of Tannerie Morel's identifiable net assets is €100 million (equal to their carrying amount).

Tannerie Morel reports a net income of €20 million in N and pays a dividend of €8 million to its shareholders in N. In N+1 it reports a net loss of €6 million and pays no dividend. No impairment is necessary.

title: Maison Vauclair – lease of a boutique
text: On 1 January N, Maison Vauclair signs a 6-year lease for a boutique in Lyon. The annual lease payment of €500 thousand is paid at the end of each year (31 December). There is no purchase option and no renewal option, and ownership is not transferred. The interest rate implicit in the lease cannot be determined; Maison Vauclair's incremental borrowing rate is 4%. Maison Vauclair pays initial direct costs of €30 thousand on signature. The right-of-use asset is depreciated on a straight-line basis.

title: LVMH – cancellation of treasury shares
text: LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton SE regularly buys back its own shares under a share repurchase programme authorised by the shareholders' meeting. The par value of an LVMH share is €0.30.

Assume that during the year LVMH bought back 1.5 million of its own shares on the market at an average price of €650 per share and that the Board of Directors then decided to cancel these 1.5 million shares, thereby reducing the share capital.
